title: POC scoping - hosted vs dedicated vs private (Orion Health)
summary: Initial POC scoping with Orion Health to agree success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, and timeline. Key decision: whether to start with Hosted for speed vs Dedicated for predictable throughput vs Private for HIPAA/PHI concerns. Security requirements (HIPAA, SOC2, KMS, SSO) discussed. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/HIPAA docs, run benchmark with 2 sample workloads week of Oct 12, deliver pricing for Hosted and Dedicated options, and draft Private deployment checklist.
topics: Benchmark plan and metrics (latency p50/p95, throughput, cost)
Deployment decision criteria: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
Meeting header: Recorded at 2026-10-07T16:00:00Z (UTC), Duration 48 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Liu (Redwood AE), Sophie Grant (Redwood SE), Alex Park (Redwood CSM) -- Mark, Priya, Liam, Rita (Orion Health)

00:00 Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side — i'm jamie, ae on the account, sophie is our solutions engineer, alex is csms, and you all?
00:15 Mark (Orion): hey, this is mark. thanks for setting this up. we wanted to scope a poc to validate performance and make a call on hosted vs dedicated vs private for our clinical inference workloads.
00:25 Jamie: great. high level, we usually try to nail down success criteria, expected qps and concurrency, sample payload sizes (tokens), and the security must-haves. then we recommend a short bench run. does that align?
00:35 Priya: yes, definitely. some context: our platform will call the model for note summarization and clinical triage — average request is ~700 tokens in, 200 tokens out. peak concurrency we expect is around 40 concurrent requests, average sustained qps ~10 with spikes to 60 for short windows.
00:53 Sophie (Redwood SE): ok that's helpful. so two workloads: 1) summarization (longer input tokens) and 2) triage/rerank (shorter, latency-sensitive). For the latency-sensitive one what are your p50/p95 targets?
01:12 Mark: for triage we'd like p50 < 150ms and p95 < 400ms if possible; summarization tolerates higher latency, p50 < 800ms. cost is also a factor, we'd like to keep unit cost reasonable.
01:28 Jamie: good callout. those latency targets push us toward lower-latency setups — dedicated capacity often gives predictable tail latency, hosted can be fine but depends on model selection and plan, private gives you full control but longer setup.
01:42 Liam (Security): quick security note — we're in healthcare, so PHI may flow through payloads. HIPAA compliance is required; we also need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), SAML SSO, audit logs, and network egress controls. we may have to do a private or VPC-hosted option for production. for a poc we could consider hosted if data is de-identified, but we need to document the risk.
02:05 Sophie: understood. for hosted we have a HIPAA offering with BAAs in certain cases — i'll flag that we need the security docs; we'll share SOC2 and HIPAA controls. for KMS, Dedicated supports customer-managed keys in our Dedicated+Private plans; for Hosted we have envelope encryption but not always customer-managed HSM by default.
02:24 Rita (Product): timeline wise, we want results to inform procurement by early November. so a 2-3 week poc starting ~Oct 12 would be ideal.
02:35 Jamie: that timeline works. typical approach we recommend: week 1 instrument and baseline (sample data, smoke tests), week 2 run benchmarks at target concurrency and collect metrics, week 3 tune batching/quantization and run final pass and cost modeling.
02:52 Mark: sounds good. what metrics will you collect during the bench?
03:00 Sophie: we'll capture p50/p95 latency, throughput (req/s), GPU utilization, token throughput, cost per 1k tokens, error rates, and memory/KV cache hit rates. we'll also provide per-route dashboards.
03:15 Priya: can you run both hosted and dedicated benchmarks in parallel? we'd like apples-to-apples.
03:22 Jamie: yes we can. for hosted we can spin up test keys and dedicated we can reserve a small pool — note dedicated lead time is a few days to provision, but it's usually faster than a full private on-prem deploy.
03:34 Mark: i want to make sure model parity is maintained — same model version, same quantization, etc. how do you handle model variants and fallback?
03:44 Sophie: we pin model versions and can run the same variant across environments. slight differences can occur due to kernel selection and quantization; we'll document the performance profile for each environment. our runtime will fallback to a compatible variant if capacity is constrained, but for benchmark we will fix the variant.
03:59 Liam: about audit logs and egress: can you keep logs within our VPC for private? and for dedicated, is egress routed through customer-managed gateway?
04:10 Jamie: private gives you full control over logging and networking. dedicated supports VPC peering and can route traffic through a customer-managed NAT/gateway; hosted has managed egress but we can restrict regions and do private networking with additional options.
04:24 Priya: for the benchmark payloads — we have a redacted dataset of ~5k records we can provide. is that enough?
04:31 Sophie: yes 5k is enough for initial bench. we'll ask for 200 samples for triage and 500 for summarization to seed the runs.
04:41 Mark: what about cost modeling? we need a per-1k token number and an estimate of monthly cost at our expected load (avg 10 qps, peak 60 qps).
04:51 Alex (CSM): we'll deliver a cost model after the bench. we'll show Hosted pricing (per-token), Dedicated commit estimates (reserved GPU cost + per-token delta), and an estimated OpEx for Private (infrastructure + license).
05:05 Rita: decision criteria checklist would be helpful — what do customers typically consider?
05:11 Jamie: yep, common buckets: 1) security/compliance needs (HIPAA/SOC2/KMS) — pushes to Private or Dedicated with specific controls; 2) latency SLOs and predictable throughput — Dedicated often; 3) speed to production and iteration — Hosted; 4) cost sensitivity — Dedicated can be cheaper if high sustained throughput; 5) operational overhead — Private requires more ops.
05:36 Mark: ok. one question: can we start POC on Hosted with de-identified data and then move to Dedicated/Private for prod?
05:44 Jamie: absolutely. that's a common path. for timelines, starting on Hosted reduces setup friction. but if you need KMS/HSM or full VPC controls for the poc, we can do Dedicated and mirror the setup.
05:55 Priya: any gotchas on tokenization differences across models? we've seen some token count variance between model forks.
06:03 Sophie: good point — we'll standardize on one tokenizer and model family for the bench, and include tokenization reproducibility checks in the pipeline.
06:12 Mark: sample benchmarks we want: 1) latency-sensitive triage at varying concurrent request levels up to 60, 2) summarization throughput with batching and KV cache enabled. also include a run with quantized weights (int8) to understand latency/cost tradeoffs.
06:31 Jamie: noted. we'll run with these knobs: batching (batch sizes), KV cache/stateful sessions, quantization profiles. we'll track cost and quality differences as well.
06:40 Liam: on quality regressions — we need regression tests tied to prompt sets. can you support eval hooks so we can measure output drift between runs?
06:49 Sophie: yes, we have eval hooks and can run golden prompts to compute embeddings similarity / rouge / vendor-appropriate metrics. we'll include that in the bench report.
06:58 Mark: great. how long between kickoff and bench results?
07:03 Jamie: plan is kickoff Oct 12, baseline by Oct 15, major bench by Oct 22, final tuning/hand-off by Oct 26. that's flexible but fits your procurement early-Nov target.
07:14 Priya: can we get an NDA/security contact? we'll need their security team to review SOC2 and HIPAA docs.
07:21 Jamie: yes i'll attach our security pack and sop. Security contact is emily thomas on our side — i'll intro you via email.
07:28 Liam: one more on procurement: if we pick Dedicated, what minimum commitment?
07:33 Jamie: Dedicated has a small monthly commit for reserved pools — for a poc we can do a short-term commit or a pilot pool; i'll include pilot pricing and what it looks like to convert to a longer-term commit.
07:44 Mark: competitors — we are also talking to Anthropic and Vertex; curious on comparisons for tail latency and cost under sustained load.
07:52 Sophie: we'll include high-level benchmark notes vs public numbers, but i can't share competitor contracts. generally Dedicated gives better tail latency; hosted varies by tier.
07:59 Rita: ok, last piece — action items and owners?
08:03 Jamie: i'll recap.

Action Items (captured verbally):
- Jamie Liu | Share SOC2 + HIPAA controls + security pack and BAA checklist | Due 2026-10-09
- Sophie Grant | Draft benchmark plan (samples needed, scripts, metrics) and provide test keys for hosted runs | Due 2026-10-10
- Mark / Priya | Provide redacted dataset and 200 triage + 500 summarization samples | Due 2026-10-09
- Alex Park | Prepare pricing for Hosted, Dedicated pilot, and Private rough estimate | Due 2026-10-12
- Jamie Liu | Schedule kickoff bench for week of 2026-10-12 and intro to security contact (Emily Thomas) | Due 2026-10-09

08:45 Jamie: any other questions?
08:48 Mark: none from me. thanks.
08:50 Jamie: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
08:52 (call ends)
